deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It is a folder cover or wrapper, most likely written by a later editor rather than by Gauss. The marks 'St I' (top right) and 'St' (below the title) are probably the siglum of Paul Stäckel, who prepared Gauss's material on the foundations of geometry and parallel theory for Werke VIII (1900). '6a' is an archival or shelf number. The pencil labels describe the contents of the enclosed sheets: 'Parallellinien' (parallel lines, i.e. the theory of parallels / non-Euclidean geometry); 'Möglichkeit der Ebene' (the possibility, i.e. existence and definition, of the plane, a topic of Gauss's foundational notes); and a third line, roughly '... Beweis/Beispiel', followed by a struck-through '87', probably a page or sheet reference. Read together, the labels say the folder holds Gauss's notes on parallels, on the existence of the plane, and a failed or tentative proof. There is no derivation to reconstruct.
